sources.summary: Human Rights Watch (29 October 2025): the leaked 11th Judicial Package would amend the penal code to criminalise conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' (up to 3 years' imprisonment), raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility, punish providers with up to 7 years and patients with up to 3, and cover symbolic same-sex ceremonies (up to 4 years); 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed it. National policy, applies in this province as everywhere else.

Kaos GL Association (24 February 2026): LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, 'The Year of the Family - A Major Siege', monitoring since 2007: 6 right-to-life violations (3 hate-motivated killings; trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 in 2024), 313 liberty violations including 299 detention decisions, 67 private-life violations (16 in 2024, a substantial share obstructing trans hormone therapy), 540 expression/assembly violations (216 in 2024) including rainbow- and trans-flag bans. National data; no province-level breakdown.

NOTE: page body not retrievable at fetch time (JS-rendered, 414 chars); per the dossier line, bianet's 31 July 2025 report covers mass ID roundups of trans women in the country's largest city - detainees filmed, one said 'this is profiling', no official reason for detention was given. Largest-city policing practice, not province-specific.

tangentialFactors: The draft 11th Judicial Package's penalties for symbolic same-sex ceremonies (up to 4 years) and the nationwide 2025 'Year of the Family' hostility campaign shape police posture toward gender-nonconforming people here as in every other province, even before the amendments are enacted.
